title: Euthyphro
author: Plato
target_audience: Readers interested in ancient Greek thought
Anyone exploring ethical and religious questions
Individuals interested in Socratic method and reasoning
primary_purpose: To explore fundamental questions about the nature of piety and the relationship between the gods and moral virtue, using Socratic questioning to probe the adequacy of traditional religious conceptions.

structure_format.organization: Single continuous dialogue between Socrates and Euthyphro, set outside the court in Athens
features: Definition and analysis of key terms

key_concepts_lessons: The importance of clear definitions in philosophical and ethical inquiry
Socratic method as a way to challenge assumptions and revealed ignorance
The 'Euthyphro dilemma': Is something pious because the gods love it, or do the gods love it because it is pious?
Religious tradition alone cannot resolve complex moral questions
Critical self-examination is necessary for understanding virtue
notable_features: Foundational text for ethics and philosophy of religion
Illustrates Socrates’ method of dialectical reasoning
cultural_historical_context: Set in Athens on the eve of Socrates’ trial, the dialogue reflects prevailing religious, legal, and philosophical concerns of classical Greece. It is among Plato’s early dialogues and sets the stage for later works exploring ethics and epistemology.
reception_impact: Regarded as a philosophical classic foundational to Western thought
The ‘Euthyphro dilemma’ remains central to debates in philosophy of religion and ethics
Widely taught and discussed in philosophy curricula worldwide
Praised for its clear exposition of Socratic questioning, but leaves the central question unresolved by design
comparable_titles: On the Nature of the Gods by Cicero
